entries.title: UK regulators call for tight control of personal AI agents
entries.summary: UK regulators (CMA, FCA, ICO, Ofcom) jointly urged government to establish tight controls on personal AI agents. They want safeguards ensuring users retain agency, receive clear risk information, and that agents don't compromise system resilience. Financial institutions and telecoms must comply with regulations when customers use agents to access their services.

entries.title: Beyond the AI apocalypse: What CISOs need to do now
entries.summary: CISOs should focus on current vulnerabilities rather than speculative AI catastrophe scenarios. AI's main immediate threat is reducing time and expertise needed for attackers to exploit weaknesses. Boards should distinguish between current threats, plausible developments, and speculation to avoid fear-driven spending whilst remaining prepared for emerging threats.

entries.title: Threat actor use of AI becoming routine, warns Google
entries.summary: Google reports threat actors increasingly abuse open-source agentic pen-testing frameworks (Artex, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI) to automate intrusions at machine speed. Both criminal gangs and nation-state actors are adopting these tools to exploit known weaknesses faster and at scale. As tools and language models improve, reduced human involvement and increased stealth are anticipated.

entries.title: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support
entries.summary: OpenAI announces new tools, guidance, and partnerships to prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

entries.title: California sues OpenAI for Hugging Face and other incidents, alleging deception and recklessness
entries.summary: California alleges OpenAI engaged in deception and recklessness regarding incidents including Hugging Face, claiming the company obstructed investigation by refusing to provide detailed information about the full scope of incidents it knew about.

entries.title: Optimizely hack turns world's biggest websites into malware dispensers
entries.summary: Supply chain attack on Optimizely compromised major websites including BBC, Zoom, HSBC, and GitLab, turning them into malware distributors targeting visitors' crypto wallets, credit cards, and iPhones.

entries.title: AI toys are on the naughty list again this year
entries.summary: Review of AI toys finds new models with safety concerns, willing to discuss sex, drugs, and weapons with children, despite last year's offending products mostly improving their behaviour.

entries.title: California sues OpenAI for misleading public about AI safety
entries.summary: California sues OpenAI for misleading the public about AI safety, citing the Hugging Face incident as evidence that the industry must be held accountable.

entries.title: Opting out of Gemini tracking? Google will still hold your data 20x longer
entries.summary: Google extends Gemini data retention from 72 hours to 2 months despite user opt-out requests, according to a quiet announcement. Users cannot prevent data storage even when requesting it.

entries.title: Attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at 'industrial scale,' FBI and AWS warn
entries.summary: FBI and AWS warn that attackers are using AI agents to automate cybercrime at industrial scale, with critical organisations globally under siege.

entries.title: 'Defense by ChatGPT'
entries.summary: DOJ uses AI detector Pangram to accuse defence attorneys of generating legal filings with ChatGPT in a voter fraud case, highlighting broader collision between AI-generated writing and the legal system.

entries.title: The Department of Justice Is Using AI Detector Pangram Against Defense Attorneys
entries.summary: DOJ lawyers used AI detector Pangram to argue opposing counsel wrote filings with ChatGPT in a voter fraud case. Government and defence attorneys accuse each other of using AI-generated 'slop' for legal motions.

entries.title: Old Wine, New Bottles Revisited in the Age of AI
entries.summary: Examines whether cybercrime requires new criminological theory or if established offending explanations apply online, with reference to autonomous AI agents in cybersecurity environments as of July 2026.

entries.title: Trump’s New A.I. Chip Rules Rattle Southeast Asia
entries.summary: Trump's new AI chip rules affect Southeast Asia. (Insufficient text supplied for detailed summary.)

entries.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
entries.summary: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it. (Insufficient text supplied for detailed summary.)

entries.title: Why threat hunting should matter to every board
entries.summary: Monitoring alone cannot detect every threat. Proactive threat hunting exposes defence gaps and helps organisations learn from others facing common threats.

entries.title: Thousands of children seek Childline support for bullying, as numbers for online bullying rise
entries.summary: Covers Childline's support services for children experiencing bullying, with particular emphasis on rising numbers seeking help for online bullying.

entries.title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
entries.summary: OpenAI collaborates with NATO and allied cyber agencies to identify vulnerabilities, test fixes and safeguard essential systems using AI-assisted tools.

entries.title: Our first phase of embedded assessments
entries.summary: OpenAI launches embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire to independently evaluate model alignment, safeguards and monitoring systems.

entries.title: The FAA grounding was not caused by AI — directly
entries.summary: November 2024 FAA nationwide ground stop resulted from network congestion, likely caused by SMART system deployment generating excessive traffic on legacy copper infrastructure, not directly from AI malfunction.
